record.text: Wrote a 2024 concurrence, joined by Justice Devine, in Hensley v. State Commission on Judicial Conduct, saying the court should have gone beyond its ruling that the judge's lawsuit could largely proceed and held that the commission lacks authority to sanction a judge who declines, for religious reasons, to perform same-sex weddings while referring couples to another officiant.

record.text: Wrote the court's October 2025 opinion in Gonzalez v. Texas Medical Board allowing a former congressional candidate, who holds a medical degree but no medical license, to proceed with claims challenging the board's cease-and-desist order over his campaign use of the titles "Dr." and "physician", without deciding the merits.

record.text: Wrote the court's June 2026 opinion in In re K.N., which affirmed termination of a mother's parental rights but held the evidence legally insufficient to support the endangerment findings against the father and sent his case back to the court of appeals, stating that a termination order "must always be a last resort and never a first impulse."

record.text: Wrote the court's September 2024 opinion in In re Dallas HERO ordering three Dallas City Council charter propositions (K, M, and N) off the November 2024 ballot because their wording did not disclose that they conflicted with, and would control over, citizen-initiated charter amendments.

Wrote a 2024 concurrence, joined by Justice Lehrmann, in State v. Zurawski, joining the court's opinion that vacated a trial court's injunction concerning the medical-emergency exception to Texas abortion laws while stressing that the Legislature holds the power to limit abortion and must write abortion laws clearly and in explicit terms.

record.text: Dissented in Ex parte Stafford (2024), in which the court held that the Election Code's "true source" provision for campaign communications violated the First Amendment, arguing that the statute could reasonably be read narrowly to bar only falsely attributing a communication to an actual person or entity.

Dissented in Finley v. State (2024), in which the court affirmed an appeals court ruling that reversed an assault conviction because the complaining witness testified wearing a surgical mask during the COVID-19 pandemic; he would have vacated that ruling and returned the case to the court of appeals.

q_county_mental.summary: Says nearly a third of people in the county jail have a mental health disorder and says he will fight to fund clinicians, detox capacity, and the Veterans Treatment Court (corrects earlier wording that described a pledge of ongoing funding for treatment courts generally).

q_ethics.summary: Says she will push for ethics reform, including stronger disclosure rules and an end to legislators voting on contracts that benefit themselves; she has not addressed campaign contribution limits, so the score is lowered from 2 to 1.

q_fossil_priority.summary: Supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy that prioritizes dispatchable power, including baseload generation standards and natural gas, nuclear, and other dispatchable sources; the score is lowered from 2 to 1 because he does not call for limiting wind or solar.
